# Sounds

Most of these are synthesized. Two are not, and their source is not recorded.

## Generated by `tools/synthesize-sounds.py`

    python3 tools/synthesize-sounds.py <outdir>
    afconvert -f m4af -d aac -b 128000 <name>.wav <name>.m4a

- the six looping beds: `white_noise`, `pink_noise`, `brown_noise`, `fan`,
  `wind`, `ocean_waves` — built sample-continuous end-to-start so they repeat
  gaplessly with no runtime crossfade
- two of the four wake tones: `singing_bowl`, `dawn` — one-shot
- `rain` is generated but not shipped (cut in review)

## Not generated, source unknown

`gentle_chime.mp3` and `soft_bells.mp3` came from the initial commit of the app
this one grew out of (December 2025), when this file was a placeholder telling
its author to add royalty-free sounds and naming freesound.org, Pixabay and
Mixkit as places to get them. Which of those they came from, and under what
licence, was never written down.

Until that is settled they should be treated as unlicensed: the repository is
MIT, and this file claimed until 16 September 2026 that every sound here was
synthesized, which was not true of these two. Replacing them with generated
tones — `tone()` builds both of the shipped tones from decaying sine partials —
is the way to make the claim true again. See `docs/spec/stir.md`, decision 22
and open 9.

`.md` files here are excluded from the app target by project.yml.
